issue.body:
Found by the stage-2 evaluation of the research report [`2026-10-05-refusal-texts-and-conditions.md`](https://github.com/diegoami/imperial-conquest-2-research/blob/593fe15/docs/reports/2026-10-05-refusal-texts-and-conditions.md) (research `593fe15`, **provisional**; promoted from ic2-conquest `970b1fe`). Literals and test order are read from the decompile **[derived: code]**; a row with a play was **seen in Wine** (box screenshot, control save, after save that differs only in UI bytes), so it is a Wine candidate until the desktop confirms it. The report's condition and effect columns are `[derived]` and its authors have **not audited** them (diegoami/ic2-conquest#58); rows that rest on those columns alone are marked so.

These are the refusals whose **outcome** differs in the clone: a guard the clone lacks (the original drops the order, the clone carries it out), or a different test order (a different line when two refusals hold). Wording alone is #801; R36, R37 and R41 (Rename and Split unit) are on #721; disbanding a regular unit away from a city is #713.

## Missing guards

| Row | The original refuses | Play | The clone |
|---|---|---|---|
| R38 | Split unit with two or more units selected: *"You can only split 1 unit at a time."* | CU03 | `godot/UI/Dialogs/ChangeUnitsDialog.cs` acts on the first selected unit (as it does for Rename, R36 on #721) |
| R39 | Split unit on a mercenary: *"You can only split regular units."* | CU02 | `SplitUnitCommandHandler` splits it; `SplitUnitCommand.cs:29–43` designs the mercenary half's name |
| R47 | Recruit unit at 100 % mobilisation: *"Your mobilisation rate is already 100%."* | RC02 | no refusal; `RecruitStandingUnitCommandHandler.cs:24–29` records it as `[open]` and only clamps the rate |
| R30 | Transfer into an army aboard a fleet whose ships are fewer than `troops / 500` after the move: *"This fleet can not carry any more troops."* (the unit stays) | TR3b | `ArmyTransferCommandHandler.cs` has no fleet-capacity test |
| P08 | Change units → Disband asks *"Are you sure you want to disband N unit."* (`units` when N > 1) and acts on every selected unit | CU07, CU08 | `ChangeUnitsDialog.DisbandSelected` (`:212`) asks nothing and disbands the first selected unit only |

## Different test order (the first failing test is the only box)

| Function | The original's order | Play | The clone's order |
|---|---|---|---|
| Join fleets | R15 (over 100 ships) before R16 (one carries an army) | **UF05c**: both hold, the 100-ship line appears | army first (`src/IC2.Engine/Naval/Commands/JoinFleetsCommandHandler.cs:79` before `:88`) |
| Repair fleet | R13 (no own city near) before R14 (carrying an army) | — | army first (`RepairFleetCommandHandler.cs:46` before `:77`) |
| Split fleet | R17 (under 20 ships) before R18 (carrying an army) | — | army first (`SplitFleetCommandHandler.cs:42` before `:50`) |
| Fortify | R22 (under siege), R23 (at 100), R24 (pending) | — | 100, pending, siege (`src/IC2.Engine/Cities/Orders/OrderCityCommandHandler.cs:59`, `:67`, `:75`) |
| Recruit mercenaries | before the dialog opens: R08 (20 units), R09 (100,000 troops), R10 (enemy city), R11 (supplies), R12 (fleet); then per hire R25 (purse), R26, R27 | — | one command: R25 (`HireMercenaryCommandHandler.cs:117`), R26 (`:125`), R08 (`:135`), R10 (`:151`), R11 (`:167`), R27 (`:178`); so a short purse is reported before low supplies or an enemy city. T113's entry already states the original's order for its dialog |

## A count

The Split army dialog counts **the nation's** armies against the 198 cap (`godot/UI/Dialogs/ArmyDialogModels.cs:353`, `:374`); the original's cap counts every army in play (`DAT_004a0324 < 0xc6`, report row R01's note and "Orders that fail without a box"), as the engine does (`SplitArmyCommandHandler.cs:69`). The engine still refuses, so only the dialog's own refusal is reached wrongly.

## Derived only (the report's unaudited columns; listed so triage can weigh them, not as confirmed)

- **Army-to-army transfer clamps per unit** (R28–R33): each selected unit is tested, last slot first; a failing unit stays and the others still move; the boxes follow the loop. The clone rejects the whole transfer (`ArmyTransferCommandHandler.cs:125`, `:134`).
- **R12**: Recruit mercenaries for an army aboard a fleet already short of space refuses before the dialog (*"Your fleet cannot carry any more troops."*); not played.
- **Disband army aboard a fleet**: the original's `TUnitMap_DisbandArmy` tests only the own city near the army (R05); the clone also refuses an army aboard (`DisbandArmyCommandHandler.cs:35`). Whether the original disbands an army aboard a fleet next to its city was not played.
- **R48**: Recruit unit at a non-capital city whose fortification is 74 or less (*"This city's fortification has fallen below 75%."*); which cities may recruit is #515.

To triage under build-process §4.8. The clone is more permissive than the original in every missing-guard row.
issue.title: Refusals the clone lacks or tests in another order: split a mercenary or several units, 100% mobilisation, a transfer onto a full fleet, Join fleets' order (research 593fe15)

comments.body: Triage (2026-10-06): row P08 split into #804 and placed in the v0.5.0 gate by the user's decision (a fix). The rest is post-v0.5.0: missing guards and test order block no normal game (§4.8). Wording follows the user's decision recorded on #801.

New evidence for the Split army cap item (stage-2 evaluation, 2026-10-08): [`2026-10-08-split-army-198-armies-cap-in-play.md`](https://github.com/diegoami/imperial-conquest-2-research/blob/main/docs/reports/2026-10-08-split-army-198-armies-cap-in-play.md), research `11157ca`, **[confirmed, partial]**, a Wine candidate. With 197 armies in play (12 AI + 185 Rome) Split army opens and the count goes to 198 at once; with 198 nothing happens. The cap is the game's army count (`DAT_004a0324`, save offset 100,956), summed over every nation, so the per-nation count at `godot/UI/Dialogs/ArmyDialogModels.cs:353` / `:374` is now contradicted in play, not only in code.

New evidence for this issue's "Derived only" row **Army-to-army transfer clamps per unit** (R28–R33): its 20-unit part is now seen in play.

[`2026-10-08-transfer-dialog-20-units-and-slot-gaps.md`](https://github.com/diegoami/imperial-conquest-2-research/blob/main/docs/reports/2026-10-08-transfer-dialog-20-units-and-slot-gaps.md), research `dc00754`, **[confirmed]** for cases c1, c4 and c5 (Wine-only, release `run-exp-transfer-20-units`):

- A target with 18 units and 3 selected source units: the two highest selected slots move (to the target's slots 18 and 19), the lowest stays, and **one** R28 box appears (c1). The second button behaves the same with R31 (c4). The test reads the target copy's slot 19 (`TArmyToArmy_Army1Transfer` :44125, `+0x750 < 1`).
- Cancel after a clamped transfer writes nothing; the dialog works on copies and only `TArmyToArmy_OK` writes them back (c5).
- R28/R31 rows of [`2026-10-05-refusal-texts-and-conditions.md`](https://github.com/diegoami/imperial-conquest-2-research/blob/main/docs/reports/2026-10-05-refusal-texts-and-conditions.md) now cite this boundary run.

The clone still rejects the whole order (`ArmyTransferCommandHandler.cs:121-125`), and `ArmyDialogModels.cs` stages units with no 20-unit check. The order in which the moved units land is filed separately as #869. The 100,000-troop part of the clamp (R29/R32) was not run.

New evidence for row R30 and the Transfer unit clamps (stage-2 evaluation, 2026-10-11): [`2026-10-09-supply-providers-and-transfer-clamps.md`](https://github.com/diegoami/imperial-conquest-2-research/blob/6b96537/docs/reports/2026-10-09-supply-providers-and-transfer-clamps.md) (research `6b96537`), section 3, **[confirmed]** (Wine) for the cases, `[code]` for the handler. Both clamps are **per unit**: the units that fit move, the others stay, and one box follows (U1: an army with 98,000 troops takes units up to **exactly 100,000**, then "An army can not hold more than 100,000 troops."; 100,000 itself is allowed). The fleet test **truncates**: it refuses only when `ships < (troops + unit) div 500`, so 30 ships take 15,499 troops (U3) and 15,500 is refused (U3b, "This fleet can not carry any more troops."); a full fleet can hold up to 499 troops over `ships x 500`. So the missing fleet-capacity test in `ArmyTransferCommandHandler.cs` should use `div 500`, not an exact `ships x 500` bound, if the fix copies the original.

Release triage: **after v0.6.0** under the user's game-breaking-only gate, recorded in https://github.com/diegoami/imperial_conquest_2/pull/1170.

Missing or reordered original refusal guards; no native save corruption or unusable essential order is established.

Full ticket list and review evidence: https://github.com/diegoami/imperial_conquest_2/pull/1170#issuecomment-6231852496

This classification leaves the issue open and does not claim a fix. A reproduced normal-game blocker returns to the release gate. Existing tests, assertions and known-failure checks remain required.
